subject: Economy
theme: Tax incentives for industrial promotion in underdeveloped regions
question_short_text: Duration of tax holiday for North-Eastern Region industries in Budget 2000
text: The Union Budget, 2000 awarded a Tax Holiday for the North-Eastern Region to promote industrialisation for:
explanation: The Union Budget 2000 introduced a 10-year tax holiday for new industrial undertakings established in the North-Eastern Region to accelerate industrialisation and promote economic development in this backward region.

research.summary: The Budget 2000 announced a ten-year tax holiday for industries set up in the North-Eastern Region under Section 80-IC of the Income Tax Act. This was a significant policy measure aimed at attracting private investment and promoting industrial development in a region that, at that time, was industrially the most backward in the country. The tax holiday was structured as a complete exemption from income tax on profits and gains for the full ten-year period, commencing from the year of production of the industrial undertaking. This provision was more generous than the standard five-year tax holiday available to small scale industries in other parts of the country, reflecting the government's commitment to regional economic development. The ten-year duration was specifically chosen to provide sufficient incentive for entrepreneurs to take on the higher risks and logistical challenges associated with establishing industries in the North-Eastern states. Unlike later schemes which bundled multiple incentives (capital investment, interest, insurance, GST reimbursement), the 2000 budget measure was a straightforward and robust income tax exemption designed to be the primary fiscal lever for attracting industry to the region.
facts: Section 80-IC was the specific provision that codified the ten-year tax holiday for North-Eastern industrial undertakings
The North-Eastern Region at the turn of the millennium had no significant manufacturing base and was heavily dependent on agriculture
The Budget 2000 was presented by Finance Minister Yashwant Sinha on February 29, 2000, and was styled as the 'Millennium Budget'
This tax holiday applied to new industrial undertakings engaged in manufacturing activities specified in the Fourteenth Schedule of the Income Tax Act
The tax holiday was available to industries in all North-Eastern states: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura
